findings.title: No code computes the paired t-tests / Bonferroni significance markers in Tables 3–5
findings.quote: We use two-tailed paired t-test with Bonferroni correction to identify statistically significant improvements
findings.claim: The paper marks nearly every UIA result in Tables 3, 4 and 5 with significance superscripts (△ ▲ ▽) from a two-tailed paired t-test with Bonferroni correction (p<0.01), but no file in the repo computes any statistical test — a grep for ttest/scipy.stats/bonferroni/wilcoxon across all .py/.ipynb/.sh returns 0 hits (see out/check_repo.csv row 1).
findings.concern: Several headline gains over the strongest baseline are tiny (e.g. Table 3 Keyword Search MRR 0.340 vs 0.336; NDCG 0.399 vs 0.392) and are only meaningful if the significance claim holds, yet the significance computation is entirely absent and unverifiable.
findings.resolution: Provide the script that computes the per-query paired t-tests and Bonferroni correction, or remove the significance superscripts.
findings.paper_ref: Sec 4.1.2 Evaluation Protocols; Table 3 caption superscripts

findings.title: Amazon ESCI 'reproducibility' dataset (Table 4) has no construction or run pipeline
findings.claim: The paper adds Amazon ESCI 'to improve reproducibility' and reports Table 4 entirely on it, but the ONLY file in the whole repo that references ESCI/amazon is this evaluator's __main__, and only as hardcoded absolute paths (see out/check_repo.csv row 2). No code implements the §4.1.1 E/S/C→three-task construction, no ESCI run script exists, and no ESCI data ships.
findings.concern: Table 4 — one of the two headline result tables and the paper's explicit reproducibility contribution (a public dataset) — cannot be reproduced from the repository.
findings.resolution: Add the ESCI download + E/S/C→(search, query-by-example, complementary) construction code, and the run/eval scripts that produced Table 4.

findings.title: No dependency specification anywhere (requirements/environment/setup)
findings.claim: A recursive glob for requirements*.txt, environment*.yml, setup.py/cfg, pyproject.toml, Pipfile and poetry.lock over the repo finds zero files; the code imports torch, transformers, faiss, ujson, yaml, pandas etc. with no pinned (or unpinned) version list.
findings.concern: The runtime environment cannot be rebuilt; faiss/transformers/torch version drift alone can change or break both indexing and results.
findings.resolution: Add a requirements.txt or environment.yml pinning at least torch, transformers, faiss, numpy, pandas, ujson, pyyaml, tqdm.

findings.title: Only README with run instructions is for a different paper (CL-DRD, SIGIR'22)
findings.quote: This repo provides code, trained models for our SIGIR'22 paper: [Curriculum Learning for Dense Retrieval Distillation](https://hansizeng.github.io/).
findings.claim: The top-level README.md contains only the UIA abstract and an architecture image (no install steps, data steps, commands, or results table). The only README that carries reproduction instructions, `kgc-dr/README.md`, documents the author's earlier CL-DRD SIGIR'22 paper and its MS MARCO pipeline — not UIA.
findings.concern: There is no README with the exact commands and results table needed to reproduce UIA's Tables 3–5; the code is a fork of the CL-DRD repo and the surviving instructions point at the wrong task and datasets.
findings.resolution: Add a UIA README giving the end-to-end command sequence (preprocess → pretrain → finetune → index → retrieve → evaluate) for at least the public ESCI dataset, with the expected metric values.

findings.title: No trained weights, ANN index, or data provided for any experiment
findings.claim: .gitignore excludes /experiments/ and /datasets/, and a scan finds no .pt/.index/.bin/.tsv/.csv artefacts checked in; the pipeline scripts assume pre-existing checkpoints and a Faiss index under an experiments/<date>/ tree that is not in the repo.
findings.concern: Retraining the two-stage BERT-base pipeline is expensive and nondeterministic across environments, so without shipped checkpoints/index the reported numbers cannot be reproduced even for the public ESCI dataset.
findings.resolution: Release the trained UIA checkpoint(s) and the built ANN index (at minimum for the public ESCI experiments), or a script that downloads them.

findings.title: Paper's validation-NDCG model/epoch selection is not implemented in the trainer
findings.claim: The paper states hyper-parameters and the number of epochs (from [8,12,16,24,48]) are chosen by validation-set NDCG, but unified_train.py runs no evaluation loop: `best_metric` (line 228) and `test_monitor` (line 119) are declared and never used, checkpoints are saved purely by step count, and only `checkpoint_latest` is exported; the curriculum trainers even comment `# not implement dev dataset` (nway_listwise_1/2/3.py). The pipeline then evaluates `checkpoint_latest` directly on the *.test.tsv qrels.
findings.concern: No validation-based selection code exists, so the reported epoch/hyper-parameter choices are unverifiable; if selection was in fact made on the test split it would be leakage (I found no evidence either way — hence medium confidence).
findings.resolution: Provide the validation-evaluation and model/epoch-selection code, and confirm selection used the validation (not test) split.
findings.paper_ref: Sec 4.1.3 ('use the model's performance on the validation set in terms of NDCG to select the hyper-parameters')

findings.title: Pipeline scripts hardcode private absolute paths (44 of 95 py/sh files)
findings.claim: The driver scripts and many modules hardcode user-specific absolute paths (/home/jupyter/unity_jointly_rec_and_search/..., /work/hzeng_umass_edu/..., /gypsum/..., /mnt/nfs/...); 44 of 95 .py/.sh files match (out/check_repo.csv row 4). Nothing is parameterised via a config or relative paths.
findings.concern: None of the training/retrieval/evaluation entrypoints run as-checked-out; a reproducer must hand-edit dozens of files, and the referenced directories are private.
findings.resolution: Replace hardcoded paths with CLI args / a config file / environment variables and provide example values.

findings.title: write_rankdata falls through into orphaned code that raises NameError
findings.claim: Inside function write_rankdata (lines 145–178), after the file-writing `with` block completes, control falls into copy-pasted orphaned code that references undefined names `self`, `qrel_path`, and `is_trec`, so every call raises NameError after writing the run file.
findings.concern: write_rankdata is called by reranking_evaluator.py:85, so the dual-encoder/cross-encoder reranking evaluation path crashes; it is broken but not on UIA's reported bi-encoder retrieval numbers.
findings.resolution: Delete the orphaned lines 162–178 (leftover from a class __init__), or move them into the intended method.

findings.title: evaluation/metrics.py has a syntax error (missing comma) and cannot be imported
findings.quote: qid, pid, rank, score = int(array[0]), int(array[1]), int(array[2]) float(array[3])
findings.claim: Line 35 is missing a comma between `int(array[2])` and `float(array[3])`, a SyntaxError that makes the whole module fail to compile (out/check_repo.csv row 3).
findings.concern: The module's recall() / recall_from_file() cannot be imported or run; impact is limited because these functions are only invoked from this file's own __main__ (not by the main RankingEvaluator used for the paper's numbers).

findings.title: divide_user_by_groups.py mixes shell into Python and uses undefined variables
findings.claim: Lines 118–145 are raw shell commands (with `\` continuations and `$VARS`) pasted into a .py file, which is a SyntaxError (out/check_repo.csv row 3); additionally lines 90–92 reference `search_uid_groups`/`sim_uid_groups`/`compl_uid_groups` that are never defined (NameError).
findings.concern: This user-grouping preprocessing script for the Lowe's data cannot run at all; it is an unfinished/broken artefact (private-data path, hence low severity).
findings.resolution: Split the shell block out of the .py file and define the *_uid_groups variables, or remove the script if it is dead.

findings.title: Sec 4.2.2 APN improvement for query-by-example (+72%) is inconsistent with Table 5
findings.quote: Using APN in UIA leads to 93%, 72%, and 145% NDCG@10 improvements in keyword search, query by example
findings.claim: Using Table 5 NDCG@10 values (UIA vs `w/o APN`): search (0.399 vs 0.207)=+92.8%≈93% ✓ and CIR (0.432 vs 0.176)=+145.5%≈145% ✓ reproduce, but query-by-example (0.495 vs 0.214) = +131.3%, not the stated +72% (see out from _audit_code/check_ablation_arith.py). The same (UIA−baseline)/baseline formula reproduces the joint-optimization 34%/45% figures exactly, so the formula is confirmed and +72% is the outlier.
findings.concern: A headline effect-size for the paper's core APN contribution is misreported (72% vs the table-implied 131%); it does not overturn the qualitative claim that APN helps greatly, but the number is internally inconsistent (likely a typo — 72.4% is what (0.369−0.214)/0.214, the wrong baseline row, would give).
findings.resolution: Recompute the query-by-example APN improvement from Table 5 and correct the 72% figure (or the underlying table value if 0.214 is the typo).
findings.paper_ref: Sec 4.2.2 Ablation Study, row 3 (w/o APN); Table 5
